nodes.name: Cu foam pretreatment
nodes.procedure: Pieces of Cu foam (1 × 2 cm²) were washed with 2.0 M HCl, ethanol, and ultrapure water, respectively, for 20 min under ultrasonication conditions to remove the grease and oxides on the surface. Subsequently, the Cu foam was dried in a vacuum oven at 55 °C for 6 h.

nodes.name: TAA-assisted electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: 0.05 mol NiCl2·6H2O and 0.01 mol thioacetamide (TAA) were added into 50 mL of deionized water (0.2 M) and the resulting transparent blue solution was used directly as the electrolyte solution. The amount of TAA was further optimized... 0.2 M is the most suitable concentration. The pre-treated Cu foam was used as the working electrode, with a graphite rod (Alfa Aesar, 99.9995%) as the counter electrode and a Hg/HgO electrode as the reference electrode. The electrodeposition was carried out at a constant voltage of -1.2 V for 200 s with a Cu foam area of 1 × 1 cm² immersed in the electrolyte. The as-prepared c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)2/CF was rinsed with ultra-pure water and ethanol, respectively, and then dried in a vacuum oven for further use.

nodes.name: Crystallization annealing
nodes.procedure: Crystalline–crystalline Ni-Ni(OH)2 (c-Ni@c-Ni(OH)2) was obtained by heat-treatment of c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)2/CF in a tubular furnace and annealed at 240 °C for 100 min in an Ar flow (100 sccm) by heating the furnace with a ramping rate of 5 °C min^-1.

nodes.name: Amorphous Ni(OH)2 electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The a-Ni(OH)2/CF was prepared by replacing the deposition solution of 0.05 mol NiCl2·6H2O with 0.1 M Ni(NO3)2. The electrodeposition was performed at a constant voltage of -0.7 V for 600 s with a Cu foam area of 1 × 1 cm² immersed in the electrolyte. It should be noted that the distance of the working electrode and the counter electrode was also controlled within the range of 2 cm.

nodes.source_text: c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)2 catalyst displays highly efficient HER activity... requiring a low overpotential of 57 mV vs. RHE to deliver -10 mA cm⁻²... Tafel slope of 44.8 mV dec⁻¹... Cdl value of 82.08 mF cm⁻²... Rct of 0.98 Ω... no noticeable degradation... for more than 27 h... After 1000 cycles, gives almost the same polarization curve.

nodes.description: HER stability after 1000 CV cycles in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: After 1000 cycles, c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)2 gives almost the same polarization curve for the HER as the original one, suggesting the excellent stability.

c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)2/CF requires a low overpotential of 411 mV vs. RHE at 50 mA cm-2, and a low Tafel slope of 70 mV dec-1. Furthermore, c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)2/CF is also highly stable for the OER in 1.0 M KOH for >10 h.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting (OWS) in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)2 exhibits remarkable OWS activity with small cell voltages of 1.608 and 1.816 V to achieve 10 and 50 mA cm-2, respectively. Moreover, c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)2 also shows good durability for OWS for at least 24 h.
c-Ni@a-NiO require much lower overpotential of 155 mV vs. RHE to deliver -10 mA cm⁻²... c-Ni@a-NiO 386 mV vs. RHE... Rct of c-Ni@a-NiO (2.56 Ω).
a-Ni(OH)2 shows a poor HER performance, requiring an overpotential of 331 mV vs. RHE to achieve a geometric current density of -10 mA cm⁻²... Rct value of a-Ni(OH)2 reaches as high as 21.51 Ω.
With the existence of the crystalline Ni core, the HER activity was improved significantly, even for the c-Ni@c-Ni(OH)2 sample with a crystalline surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)₂ and c-Ni@a-NiO show Ni peaks at 44.5°, 51.8°, 76.3° (JCPDS 04-0850); no Ni(OH)₂ or NiO peaks due to amorphous nature. c-Ni@c-Ni(OH)₂ shows both Ni and Ni(OH)₂ peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)₂ and c-Ni@a-NiO, the diffraction peaks at 44.5, 51.8, and 76.3° can be well indexed to... Ni (JCPDS 04-0850), whereas the characteristic XRD peaks for Ni(OH)₂, NiO... are not detected because of their amorphous feature. In contrast, the diffraction peaks belonging to Ni and Ni(OH)₂ are observed simultaneously for c-Ni@c-Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman bands at ~320, 490 cm⁻¹ (A₁g(T), E_g(T) phonons) and ~800 cm⁻¹ (E_g(R) mode) confirm Ni(OH)₂; NiO shows TO at ~500 cm⁻¹, 2TO/2LO at ~710/1080 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)₂, the Raman bands centered at ~320 and 490 cm⁻¹ are identified as the translational A₁g(T) and E_g(T) phonons... typical NiO vibrational modes are observed for c-Ni@a-NiO, namely one-phonon scattering (TO mode) at ~500 cm⁻¹...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p for Ni(OH)₂ samples (c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)₂, c-Ni@c-Ni(OH)₂, a-Ni(OH)₂): Ni²⁺ at 855.7/873.3 eV (spin-orbit separation 17.6 eV). c-Ni@a-NiO: 854.5/872.8 eV (18.3 eV) for NiO. O 1s: c-Ni@a-NiO shows Ni-O (529 eV) and Ni-OH (531 eV); other samples lack Ni-O peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the Ni 2p of c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)₂, c-Ni@c-Ni(OH)₂ and a-Ni(OH)₂... two peaks at... 855.7 and 873.3 eV correspond to... Ni²⁺... spin-energy separation... 17.6 eV, which is an important criterion for... Ni(OH)₂. In contrast, for the c-Ni@a-NiO sample... 854.5 and 872.8 eV... spin-energy separation of 18.3 eV which is reported as evidence for... NiO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Core shows crystalline Ni with 2.03 Å lattice fringe (Ni(111)); surface exhibits amorphous layered nanosheet feature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the core part, the HRTEM image... indicate a highly crystalline feature, with a distinct lattice fringe of 2.03 Å corresponding to the Ni(111) plane. In contrast, the layered surface zone shows the characteristic of amorphous materials.
